reasoning: The extract has no real success measures, testing or evaluation plan for the 6% GHG reduction obligation, but it does set out a review timetable. Regulation 26 is described as requiring the Secretary of State to "review the Regulations, assess the extent to which the Regulations have achieved their objective and publish a report of the findings no more than five years after they have come into force" (line 7). The proposal is to review "by no later than five years after the planned in-force date, which would be by no later than April 2022" (lines 5 and 10). That is a timetable with a commitment to publish a report, and it hints at an evaluation question: whether the objective was achieved. It also says "The UK is required to report progress towards the target to the European Commission annually" (line 2), which is a reporting mechanism. Against that, the document names no outcomes to be measured, no indicators, no testing before rollout and no reasons for omitting testing. Reference 5, an ICCT report on flaring and venting, has no bearing on evaluation. The strongest case for a higher level is the dated review with a published report, but without success measures or testing this sits at level 1. To reach level 2 it would need to state which outcomes will be measured (for example, actual GHG intensity reductions), describe how the review will assess them, and say whether testing or piloting was considered. Level 3 would also need reasons for those choices and clear plans for publishing the results.
